_about: Cross-claims the layers standing check accepts (tests/layersStanding.test.ts): a layered row of <category> that <claimed_by>'s mapping also places by a SKU rule. Each group is recorded with its exact row count — a new group, a grown or shrunk count, or a stale entry fails the check. Statuses: claimant-rule-too-broad (fix in that category's round), decided-home (a decision placed the family here), pending-round (the home is decided in the named round), pending-decision:Q-<n> (kept where filed while that open question is answered — re-audit decisions, operator, 15 Sep 2026, F-6; the status is stale once the question closes).

entries.reason: The same merge (run 1204): the Meeting Server appliances themselves. Their pre-merge home was conferencing, whose mapping file is retained for the status table and still names them — a claim from a category that now holds nothing, not a rival home.

UCSC-C240-M8-CL(-G) arrived from conferencing in the merge (run 1204): a C240 M8 sold as the collaboration appliance, so every mapping that reads a 240 platform token claims it. One home per SKU, and the merge decided this one; the HCI node series is a rival reading of the same token, not a second home.

CIT3-5108-PKG-HW arrived from conferencing in the merge (run 1204): the packaged 5108 chassis of a Meeting Server deployment, so the servers mapping reads its 5108 token. The merge decided its home; this is the platform it is built on, not a rival filing.

CIT3- rows arrived from conferencing in the merge (run 1204). They are Cisco Meeting Server appliances BUILT ON a UCS B200 blade, so the servers mapping reads the B200 token in their SKU; the operator's merge decided that a conferencing appliance is a collaboration endpoint, which is where the row lives.

The same two rows read by the servers mapping's own C240 rule. Recorded separately because the leakage scan groups by claiming RULE, so one row claimed by two rules is two groups — and a count that silently merged them would hide either rule changing.

TWO DECISIONS MET HERE AND THE LATER ONE STANDS. The interfaces-modules round (14 Sep 2026, item 7) gave every NIM / SPA / EPA / HWIC / PVDM / VIC / SM-X card one home, interfaces-modules, and its plan ran (run #1068). The re-audit then planned the ASR 1000-ONLY SPAs back to routers under A.3 rule 1 (a card bound to one platform lives with its platform), and that plan ran on 16 Sep (run #1174). So these three rows sit in routers, placed by the ASR 1000 series rule, while the interfaces-modules ^SPA- rule still claims every SPA- PID: one home per SKU, and the home is routers. The operator may prefer the earlier blanket rule — it is a question about the SPA family, not about these rows' placement (implementer, operator's 12-hour delegation, 16 Sep 2026)
